A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ATST-MDP framework and learning algorithm. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching results moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical results, mathematical examples, and proofs. Neither its main text nor its appendices report original experiments or simulations.

after.justification: V2 Section 6 reports original RiverSwim and RiverBalance simulations. Figure 3 presents learning curves averaged over five simulations.

M1.justification: The core LSVI-UCB procedure remains, renamed ATST-LSVI-UCB. V2 adds an implementation restricted to finite, eventually periodic action-sequences, with closed-form feature computation, and guards the observation-probability estimator against zero sample counts. Algorithm 1 also restores a feature multiplier already present in v1's Appendix D; this is a pseudocode correction rather than a new regression update.

E1.justification: V1 has no empirical task coverage. V2 evaluates two six-state, two-action environments: RiverSwim tests exploration toward a distant reward, while the new RiverBalance task requires repeated state-dependent corrections to remain near rewarding central states.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing algorithms. V2 Figure 3 compares ATST-LSVI-UCB across observation probabilities; cited LSVI-UCB, POMDP, and active-observation methods do not participate as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: V2 introduces an experimental protocol using gamma=0.99, uniform observation probabilities of 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, and 0.5, exact action-sequence features, H=100, and 1,012 candidate sequences. Figure 3 measures the (1-gamma)-scaled running average of episodic reward. These are new evaluation settings; the theoretical interaction protocol largely persists.

E4.justification: Section 6 adds the first systematic observation-frequency sensitivity analysis. Varying observation probability in both environments tests how sparse feedback affects exploration versus corrective control. V1 contains no corresponding empirical sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 3 newly reports averaging over five simulations. It provides no confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or seed identifiers. V1 has no empirical repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds the learning curves in Figure 3: smaller observation probabilities produce faster RiverSwim learning, whereas larger probabilities produce higher RiverBalance reward plateaus. These are new simulation findings, not improvements over corresponding v1 measurements.

T1.justification: The central Bellman, linearity, estimation, and regret results persist. V2 adds a spectral-radius bound and the periodic-sequence closed form with proof (Lemmas C.4 and C.12), and corrects auxiliary bounds in Appendices C–D. Its sufficient feature accuracy changes from O((1-gamma)/K) to O((1-gamma)/(K sqrt(d))), increasing the displayed sample requirement's dimension factor from d^3 to d^4. The explicit linear encodings in v1 Examples 2.3–2.4 are removed.

C1.justification: V2 adds empirical validation and observation-frequency/task interactions to its stated contributions. The principal claims about the ATST-MDP framework, linear action-sequence representation, feature estimation, and conditional regret guarantee remain.

C2.justification: V2 introduces explanations linking sparse observations to longer exploration commitments in RiverSwim and frequent observations to corrective control in RiverBalance. It also explicitly interprets feature estimation as reward-free and reusable across reward functions, and distinguishes the beta-dependent optimal value from the uniform regret bound. The oracle and fully online estimation limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies experimental implementation details absent from v1: transition/reward diagrams, candidate-sequence prefix and period bounds, the 1,012-candidate count, exact-feature access, and H=100. Appendix C.4 provides the feature-computation formula and O((P+L)d^3) cost. No code-access or hardware information is added.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands and refines positioning through POMDP hardness, impaired observability, episodic reward delays, and delayed online/bandit/convex optimization. It explicitly identifies ACNO-MDPs as a strict special case and corrects v1's characterization of goal-conditioned RL as withholding state observations. Bibliographic updates to retained works are separate from these substantive changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and much of the main exposition are rewritten. V2 separates the problem setting, augmented-state analysis, linear representation, and learning algorithm into a clearer progression; it condenses preliminary material, removes worked examples, and reorganizes feature estimation. The algorithm name and author information also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds two-panel environment diagrams in Figure 2 and two-panel learning curves in Figure 3; v1 contains only the interaction-protocol figure. Algorithm 1 gains explicit planning/execution divisions, and the document adopts denser typography and a different page format throughout the main text and appendices.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity and internal consistency through reorganized explanations and corrected algorithm and appendix equations. The proved periodic-sequence construction and simulations add useful implementation guidance and evidence about observation-frequency tradeoffs. The gains remain limited around unchanged principal guarantees: experiments use exact features, omit variability estimates, and provide no optimal-policy reference supporting the new near-optimality interpretation.
